use_it_for.text: Landing-pad, regolith-handling and construction trials on flat barren ground.
Instrument and habitat thermal-cycling tests in large day-night temperature swings.
Dust-mitigation tests for seals, solar panels and suits.
Life-detection instrument tests at the dry limit of life (biosignature preservation).

habitability.text: Mars once had lakes and still holds ground ice, so it may have been habitable. Earth analogs help test how to recognise signs of past or present life in rock and soil.
Hyper-arid: soils this dry hold very little life, so life-detection instruments can be tested against a nearly lifeless background, as in the Atacama.
Over 90% bare ground: plants do not hide the surface, so sensors see rock and soil much as they would on the Moon or Mars.

breaks_down.text: Gravity is 0.38x Earth: Earth tests overload structures, wheels and people.
Surface pressure is 0.01x this place: no Earth site reproduces vacuum or the thin Martian air (heat transfer, dust lofting, boiling).
Surface radiation dose is 97.4x Earth: Earth's atmosphere and magnetic field shield every analog site.
Caves, lava tubes and other underground environments are not assessed: satellite data see only the surface. Documented cave and mine analogs are listed in the findings.
Day-night surface temperature swing: the target value (70) is outside the middle 98% of Earth's sampled values; this place gets 33% of the way from Earth's typical value.
Coldest night surface temperature: the target value (165) is outside the middle 98% of Earth's sampled values; this place gets 15% of the way from Earth's typical value.
Mean temperature: the target value (-73) is outside the middle 98% of Earth's sampled values; this place gets 3% of the way from Earth's typical value.
Coldest-season temperature: the target value (-100) is outside the middle 98% of Earth's sampled values; this place gets 10% of the way from Earth's typical value.
